title: Runtime Store Foundation
goal: Reduce frontend drift risk before larger UI surfaces land by introducing a thin runtime-store seam around shared state without starting a framework rewrite.
scope: Implement the first frontend state-architecture slice by adding a minimal store or event-bus seam around shared runtime state, moving the most mutation-heavy wizard and Mission Control paths onto that seam, and documenting the exit criteria for any future broader migration. Keep React, Vue, Preact, or full-shell rewrites out of scope.
generation_reason: Anti-drift hardening for the repo-backed post-intake backlog.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not promote or implement this task until the current task in NEXT_TASK.md is completed and logged.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Keep this slice to a thin state seam and direct-mutation reduction. Defer framework migration, shell redesign, and unrelated feature work.
notes: Preserve existing DOM ids, test ids, and supported UI behavior.
Introduce a small store API such as getState, patchState, and subscribe rather than adopting a full framework in this slice.

success_criteria: A minimal runtime-store seam exists and becomes the supported path for shared wizard and Mission Control state updates.
Wizard and Mission Control stop mutating the shared runtime object directly in the most churn-prone paths covered by this slice.
Existing UI tests remain green with the new store seam in place.
Documentation captures the specific exit criteria that would justify a future broader reactive-layer migration.
No new product feature is bundled into this architecture slice.

acceptance_criteria: The store seam reduces direct shared-state mutation in the targeted modules without changing supported behavior.
The slice does not add a framework dependency or product-surface redesign.
The repo gains explicit migration exit criteria instead of vague future-reactivity notes.

before_promotion: The active conversational-intake task in NEXT_TASK.md is completed, logged, and removed from active status.
python3 scripts/validate_backlog_tasks.py passes with this package still queued.
No framework migration or unrelated UI feature bundle is attached to the same promotion.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with the runtime-store seam slice and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the new state-management baseline and any remaining drift risks.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md and rerun python3 scripts/validate_backlog_tasks.py.
